title: Let foreign branch losses count against UK tax again
noun: letting foreign branch losses count again
headline: Allow foreign branch losses. Costs £0.5bn in 2029-30.
description: From January 2027 every foreign branch of a UK company is exempt from UK corporation tax, so its losses can no longer cut the UK bill either. Switch this on to drop the change.

baselinePolicy.text: The foreign permanent establishment exemption is mandatory from 1 January 2027 (Table 6.1 line 68).

source.quote: so foreign branch profits will be exempt from UK Corporation Tax and foreign branch losses will no longer be available to offset UK taxable profits

alreadyIncludes: The foreign permanent establishment exemption is mandatory from 1 January 2027 (Table 6.1 line 68).

lines.title: Corporation Tax: Make the foreign permanent establishment exemption mandatory, preventing their losses from reducing UK corporation tax receipts for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2027

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury’s costing with its sign reversed (positive scorecard values reduce borrowing; here receipts positive means more revenue).

caveats: The Treasury’s costing is on the OBR October 2026 forecast, the baseline used here. Effects before the start year are not applied: 2026-27 falls before any Budget of yours.

considerations.text: The Treasury’s scorecard figure is the certified direct costing for the measure, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed; the Budget 2026 policy costings document gives the method.
